harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (an OPNsense/FreeBSD appliance acting as the private-network's resolver via its built-in Unbound service) to block blocked.example and all its subdomains with a persistent local-zone always_nxdomain drop-in (/usr/local/etc/unbound.opnsense.d/[REDACTED].conf, loaded by OPNsense's start.sh on every boot/reload), while all other names continue to resolve normally. Pointed node2 and node3 (Alpine) at node1 (10.100.40.10) for DNS by writing /etc/resolv.conf and disabling dhcpcd's resolv.conf hook so the setting survives reboots. Verified apex and subdomain queries for blocked.example return NXDOMAIN and unrelated domains (e.g. example.com) resolve correctly from node1 itself and from both node2 and node3. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (preserving no shared quorum requirement since this is a resolver+2 clients topology), confirmed each node's boot identity changed (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3), and re-verified DNS blocking/resolution health after each restart. Node3 took an unusually long time (~35 minutes of polling with persistent "connection reset by peer") to become reachable again after `reboot`, but it did fully recover with all configuration and behavior intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 and identified it as an OPNsense/FreeBSD image running Unbound as the active DNS resolver on port 53 (dnsmasq present but not the active DNS listener)
Created /usr/local/etc/unbound.opnsense.d/[REDACTED].conf on node1 with 'local-zone: "blocked.example." always_nxdomain' and restarted Unbound via configctl
Verified NXDOMAIN for blocked.example, sub.blocked.example, deep.sub.blocked.example from node1's loopback resolver, and normal resolution for example.com
Confirmed OPNsense's default LAN pass rule already permits DNS (UDP/TCP 53) from the shared 10.100.40.0/24 network to node1
Updated node2 and node3 /etc/resolv.conf to use nameserver 10.100.40.10 and added 'nohook resolv.conf' to /etc/dhcpcd.conf so the setting persists across DHCP renewals/reboots
Verified from node2 and node3 (using default system resolver, no explicit server argument) that blocked.example and subdomains return NXDOMAIN while example.com resolves normally
Captured pre-restart baselines: node1 kern.boottime, node2 and node3 /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, plus live proof of DNS health on all three

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect; polled until exec was available again; confirmed kern.boottime changed and Unbound/blocking/resolution recovered
Restarted node2 via backgrounded 'reboot'; confirmed boot_id changed and resolv.conf/DNS blocking/resolution recovered

Restarted node3 via backgrounded 'reboot'; polled extensively (~35 minutes, persistent 'connection reset by peer') until it recovered; confirmed boot_id changed and resolv.conf/DNS blocking/resolution recovered
Final cross-check on node1 confirming Unbound still healthy and blocking/resolution correct after all three node restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 resolves normal names for node2/node3 network
evidence.summary: node1's Unbound resolver answers example.com with real A/AAAA records both locally and when queried from node2/node3

evidence.requirement: blocked.example and all subdomains resolve to nothing usable from both node2 and node3
evidence.summary: Custom unbound.opnsense.d config added always_nxdomain local-zone for blocked.example.; verified NXDOMAIN for apex, sub, and deep.sub queries from node1 loopback and from node2/node3 via their system resolver pointed at node1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to use node1 as DNS server persistently
evidence.summary: Set /etc/resolv.conf nameserver to 10.100.40.10 and disabled dhcpcd's resolv.conf hook on both node2 and node3
Captured kern.boottime=1788625960 and confirmed blocking config file present pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out then succeeded with kern.boottime=1788626215 (changed); Unbound process, blocked-domain NXDOMAIN, and normal resolution all confirmed recovered, re-verified again after later node restarts

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; connection reset then recovered with boot_id=3ab41865-ce63-432a-9ae0-1bf44fd448ae (changed); resolv.conf persisted and blocked/normal DNS resolution confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; after an unusually long ~35-minute polling period with persistent connection resets, node recovered with boot_id=b5b17dd7-2440-4dc2-b247-4067aaf3dbf4 (changed); resolv.conf persisted and blocked/normal DNS resolution confirmed recovered
